content.text: {"steps":[{"id":"s1","description":"Use list_documents, then read candidate_specs.md. Extract the three allowed radiator candidates, assign numeric IDs 1–3 for later reference, and record each candidate’s relevant numeric properties, including allowed/nominal thickness range if given and refractive-index-related quantities needed for 10 GeV/c pion/kaon separation."},{"id":"s2","description":"Read the project document(s) describing humidity ageing or transparency tests. For each of the three candidates, extract the 10-year-equivalent transparency loss percentage and record it. Mark candidates with transparency loss greater than 10% as failing the hard ageing requirement."},{"id":"s3","description":"Read the simulation documentation/results for RICH pion/kaon separation at 10 GeV/c versus radiator material and thickness. For each candidate, evaluate or extract the predicted separation over the allowed 1–6 cm thickness range, with enough thickness points to identify the best-performing allowed thickness, and record the maximum separation and corresponding thickness."},{"id":"s4","description":"Apply the hard cuts: candidate must be one of the three listed, thickness must be between 1 and 6 cm, transparency loss must be at most 10%, and pion/kaon separation at 10 GeV/c must be at least 3.5 sigma. Record numeric pass/fail indicators for each candidate for ageing and separation."},{"id":"s5","description":"Among candidates passing all hard requirements, select the radiator and thickness with the highest simulated pion/kaon separation at 10 GeV/c. Record the selected candidate ID, selected thickness in cm, predicted separation in sigma, and transparency loss percentage for use by the reporting module."}]}
